documents.title: Fictional Lumen depot closure manual, revision 4

paragraphs.1: This fictional manual governs only administrative closure of domestic depot transfer cases. It neither orders payment nor establishes that a supplier caused a delay. A transfer case is a file collecting a handover, ledger evidence, and review records. Closure marks that file administratively complete. All examples and organizations in this packet are invented. Foreign transfers, employee matters, and purchasing approvals are outside scope. Review staff may use a dashboard as an index, but a dashboard badge is not itself a governing policy.
paragraphs.2: For every domestic case, closure requires a reconciled quantity and a valid handover. These two requirements are necessary; this paragraph does not say that together they are sufficient. Reconciliation means the signed depot count equals the dispatched count for the same case identifier. Handover validity is specified in the registry annex, not by the title of an uploaded file. The old practice of treating a green progress bar as a signed handover is not incorporated here.
paragraphs.3: For routine cases, reconciled quantity, valid handover, and a cleared settlement jointly suffice for closure, provided no active hold exists. For exception cases, reconciled quantity, valid handover, an exception waiver, and a completed audit jointly suffice for closure, provided no active hold exists. Either route is a sufficient route only for its stated class. The exception route does not require cleared settlement. No other closure route is authorized by this manual. A missing condition should not be converted into a negative fact merely because a user interface leaves a cell empty.
paragraphs.4: An active hold forbids closure even when every positive condition of a route is present. An explicitly inactive hold does not contribute any affirmative evidence about settlement or handover. The hold list is maintained outside the dashboard. Staff sometimes annotate a file as ready before a hold is removed; ready is a scheduling label, not permission to close. If the authoritative hold status is unavailable, neither the ready label nor absence of a local note settles it.
paragraphs.5: For routine cases only, cleared settlement is necessary for closure. Cleared settlement is not a universal requirement for exception cases. Closure is neither sufficient nor necessary for payment authorization: payment is governed by a separate policy not supplied in this packet. The table headed payment_status is included for routing queries and must not be treated as that missing policy. Closing a file alone also says nothing about the cause of a service-level change.

documents.title: Fictional registry and event dictionary, edition 2

paragraphs.1: The registry supplies case_id, case_class, signed_count, dispatched_count, handover_signature, receiving_role, receipt_date, posting_date, settlement_flag, and a legacy local_handover flag. case_id is the join key. case_class is either routine or exception. The signature and role belong to the same handover event. A valid handover requires the signature of the receiving lead; a driver signature does not satisfy this definition. For this packet the receiving-lead signature on the linked handover is sufficient for handover validity. Scan filenames and upload dates cannot substitute for event linkage.
paragraphs.2: receipt_date records the date funds reached the collection bank. posting_date records the date the ledger entry was posted. Export columns also include settlement_flag with values Y, N, and blank. The field-description cell for settlement_flag in this edition reads "see settlement interface specification SI-9". SI-9 is not among the supplied documents. An independent attestation explicitly stating cleared settlement can establish that fact. Bank receipt and ledger posting events can occur on different days, including across a month boundary. Corrections to posting entries keep their original receipt reference so the two event streams can be reconciled later.
paragraphs.3: The optional dashboard column paid_at is shown in several screenshots, including exports that also contain receipt_date and posting_date. The registry gives its owner as the dashboard migration team and leaves the semantic-definition and timezone cells blank. The dashboard user guide describes column width, sorting, and how to export visible rows. Local analysts use the dashboard to locate cases before checking the event registry. Some rows happen to display the same date in all three columns; others do not. The packet includes neither the migration mapping sheet nor a signed definition for paid_at.
paragraphs.4: The archive contains a quick-reference card from revision 3. It said a driver-signed local_handover record was enough for valid handover, and that an exception waiver could replace an audit. The card remains visible for historical interpretation of old records. The revision-4 manual and this registry govern new records from 2032-04-01 onward. A new record may carry a copy of the card, but that attachment alone does not give the card current authority. Historical reporting should preserve the policy version used rather than rewriting old events.
